vectors.description: Interrupted publication is recovered before watch registration, but the current session still requires its own admitted initial build.
An inline option value ending in .hxml is compiled through one private checked input that is removed before validation and never enters public output.
An initial compiler failure publishes nothing, keeps firstAccepted pending, and a later valid revision becomes generation 1.
A rejected initial candidate remains private and a later admitted candidate becomes the first public generation.
After generation 1, a compiler failure leaves that generation public and reports a degraded state.
A host-rejected candidate never reaches public output and the earlier admitted generation remains usable.
Twenty observed edits during revision 1 produce no overlap, discard its known-stale candidate, and run one revision 21 follow-up.
A client subscribes before an owned-server fallback and inspects afterward; the snapshot retains the exact fallback while the accepted generation records direct mode.
A publication waits for an active generated-file read and emits no accepted event until the reader releases its lease and commit finishes.
A publication failure restores the exact prior generated output, prepared input, and validator receipt; it retains generation 1 and reports a degraded publish-phase failure.
Prepared input and a validator receipt publish with generation 1; generation 2 updates the prepared input and removes the now-absent receipt in the same accepted update.
An admitted candidate with identical public bytes advances the accepted snapshot without writing files or asking a host to reload.
A fatal inventory error before watch registration rejects firstAccepted and publishes no output.
Closing during the initial build rejects firstAccepted, discards queued work, and a repeated close emits no duplicate lifecycle events.
